question: Why did the error rate go up on 07 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: Upstream search-cluster is returning HTTP 503 and experiencing timeouts.
why_chain: The upstream search-cluster is the source of the error rate increase.
The search-cluster is returning HTTP 503, indicating a service failure.
The search-cluster is experiencing timeouts, causing retries and increased latency.

contributing_factors.description: Request volume for service search is increasing, but not enough to explain the error rate increase.
why_chain: The error rate increase is concentrated in service search, not all services.
The request volume for service search is only slightly higher after the change.
The error rate increase is more pronounced than the request volume increase.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate increase is due to a configuration change.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a configuration change.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate increase is due to a data issue.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a data issue.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate increase is due to a deployment issue.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate increase is after the deployment, not before.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service search rose from 0.35% to 3.74% (+965%), with a change point at 2026-03-07T05:30:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service search: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.12).
At the same time, request volume for service search stayed about the same (2454 per 5 min before, 2862 per 5 min after, +17%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service search rose (141 ms before, 253 ms after, +80%).
Upstream search-cluster returning HTTP 503 for search (search; 2 min after the change; record R014)
search: ERROR upstream search-cluster timeout after 3 retries (search, us-east; 5 min after the change; record R015)
search: ERROR upstream search-cluster timeout after 3 retries (search, ap-south; 10 min after the change; record R016)
search: ERROR upstream search-cluster timeout after 3 retries (search, eu-west; 19 min after the change; record R017)
search-cluster status page: investigating degraded performance (search; 30 min after the change; record R018)

reasons: ✓ A change event (alerts) lines up in time (2 min after the change).
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Contact the upstream search-cluster team to investigate the service failure and timeouts.
Monitor the upstream search-cluster and take immediate action if it shows signs of failure again.
Review and optimize the request handling logic for service search to better handle increased load.
